title: Resolve asymmetric HTTPS proxy egress rewrite causing tenant DNS overrides after peering failover
creator: Ethan Zhao
description: Several Dedicated tenants observed transient DNS responses for internal hostnames resolving to other tenants' egress IPs after VPC peering flaps. Root cause traced to an asymmetric rewrite path in the edge HTTPS proxy during peering failover: a small window where outbound connections were NATed by a stale SNAT mapping on the original node, while DNS responses were served from the new peer, causing short-lived cross-tenant name resolution and client confusion. This ticket tracks the fix, validation, and rollback plan.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger controlled peering flap between two tenant VPCs in staging (simulate BGP/peering disruption)
Issue a burst of HTTPS requests from a long-lived tenant session that uses the edge HTTPS proxy and observes egress SNAT mapping
During the flap, attempt DNS resolution for an internal tenant service from a different tenant and observe mismatched A records returned intermittently
Correlate with conntrack / NAT table dumps on edge nodes and proxy logs to reproduce the mapping window
investigation_notes: 03/01: Initial customer report from AcmeAI - intermittent 502s and service misrouting correlated with peering failovers.
03/02: Captured conntrack and iptables NAT tables during a staged failover; observed stale SNAT entries persisted ~7-12s after route reparenting.

03/03: Edge HTTPS proxy logic applies an egress-rewrite for tenant egress tracking. During failover the proxy continued to reuse a cached outbound socket bound to previous SNAT, while DNS requests were routed via the new node.
03/04: Hypothesis: asynchronous cache invalidation between routing layer and proxy socket leasing causes transient cross-tenant egress identity exposure.
03/05: Reproduced in staging with adjusted kernel conntrack timeout; mismatch window reduced when conntrack expiration was shortened.
03/06: Reviewed historical incident ENG-71102 for similar SNAT affinity timing but behavior here differs due to HTTPS proxy socket reuse and DNS TTL interplay.

03/07: Decided to implement three-pronged mitigation: (1) force proxy socket rebind on detected route change, (2) tighten conntrack garbage collection for ephemeral tenant mappings, (3) add DNS resolution affinity checks in the control-plane sanity layer.
mitigation: Hotfix 1 (staging): Proxy change to mark outbound socket as stale on peering-change hook and re-open connection (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1974)
Hotfix 2 (staging): Kernel-level conntrack tuning added as emergency knob for affected host pools (playbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/conntrack-tuning)
Temporary customer mitigation: Instructed impacted tenants to reduce aggressive DNS TTLs and enabled per-tenant egress pinning for mission-critical traffic
proposed_fix_details: Ensure edge proxy subscribes to route change events from the node agent and performs deterministic socket rebinds when egress path changes.
Update the node-agent to emit a peering-state-change event and include a revision token used by the proxy to validate active egress identity.
Introduce a short-lived tenant egress lease (server-side) that invalidates NAT bindings within 2s on detected reparenting to limit exposure window.
Add unit + integration tests: peering-change simulation harness, conntrack inspection assertions, and DNS resolution consistency checks.
Rollout strategy: staged canary on dedicated pool with traffic shadowing, 24-48h observation window, automatic rollback on regression metric spike.
acceptance_criteria: No cross-tenant DNS/A-record mismatches observed in staged peering-failover tests across 1000 simulated sessions
Proxy rebinds occur within 1s of node-agent peering-state-change event in 99.9% of cases
No increase in proxy CPU/memory beyond 5% during rebind storms (load test validated)
Customer-facing incidents related to this root cause reduced to zero for 7 days on canary pool before full rollout
risks_and_tradeoffs: Forcing socket rebinds increases short-term connection churn which may raise tail latency for active sessions; mitigated by graceful drain logic and backoff
Aggressive conntrack GC can increase packet churn and may impact throughput on very high connection-rate tenants; we will only apply tuned settings to affected host pools initially
Adding additional control-plane events increases coupling between node-agent and proxy; design aims for idempotent, versioned events to reduce brittleness
testing_plan: Unit tests for proxy socket lifecycle and node-agent event handling
Integration test in staging: automated peering flap script that runs 10k sessions and verifies DNS/ejection consistency
Load test with 2x baseline QPS to validate resource impact
Run a 48-hour canary on a non-critical dedicated pool with real tenant traffic and enhanced logging
